newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan likely to test ship nuclear waste to Russia.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan likely to test ship nuclear waste to Russia.

text.p: Taiwan is likely to test ship 5,000 barrels of its nuclear waste to Russia after failing to find a new location at home, an official of state Taiwan Power Company said on Monday.
"Both sides have the willingness and if we can sign a contract, we will ship 5,000 barrels to Russia as a test," the official said by telephone.
"It will be just a test for us to see whether we can have a long-term deal with Russia," he added.
Taiwan decided in July to stop sending nuclear waste to tiny Lanyu island, its only nuclear waste dump, following strong protests by aboriginals there.
Since 1982, Taiwan has stored 97,672 barrels of nuclear waste at the Lanyu dump which has a capacity of 98,112 barrels.
Taiwan Power has promised to remove all the nuclear waste in Lanyu by 2002 and it has been seeking sites overseas, including China, the Marshall Islands and Russia.
"Russia is the most possible place so far although we have not signed any agreement with them," the official said. He added that there had been no timetable for an agreement.
It was not clear how much Taiwan would pay Russia for taking the nuclear waste.
Taiwan Power offered in August to pay T$3.2 billion (US$116 million) to local governments and residents in Taiwan if they could offer a dump for the nuclear waste.
Taiwan currently has three nuclear power plants and the government plans to build the fourth one in the northern county of Taipei.
